stages.name: Roman province
stages.desc: Governed by a Roman proconsul or legate (Syria, Cilicia–Cyprus, Cyrenaica, then Egypt)

stages.name: Ptolemaic kingdom
stages.desc: Ruled from Alexandria by Cleopatra, including the lands Caesar and Antony gave her

stages.name: Free cities
stages.desc: Self-governing cities under Rome's protection: Tyre and Sidon

stages.name: Client kingdoms
stages.desc: Local kings and princes ruling with Rome's consent: Judaea, Nabataea, Ituraea

stages.name: Parthian occupation
stages.desc: Held by the armies of Pacorus and Labienus, or by kings they installed

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Annexed by Rome in 58 BC and governed with the province of Cilicia
Caesar hands Cyprus back to the Ptolemies; it soon answers to Cleopatra
Cleopatra's governor Serapion sends the island's ships to help Cassius
Antony confirms Cyprus, with its copper and shipyards, as Cleopatra's
With Cleopatra dead, Cyprus returns to Roman rule

states.name: Israel
timeline: Hyrcanus II is high priest of a reduced Judaea; Antipater the Idumaean holds real power
Caesar rewards Hyrcanus and Antipater for their help in Egypt and returns Joppa to Judaea
Herod, Antipater's son, drives Marion of Tyre out of Galilee
The Parthians make the Hasmonean Antigonus king; Herod flees
Herod, named king by the Roman Senate, takes Jerusalem with Roman legions
Antony gives Cleopatra coastal lands of Herod's kingdom; Herod keeps the interior
An earthquake strikes Judaea; Herod fights the Nabataeans for Antony
Octavian confirms Herod and gives him Gaza, Joppa and the coastal cities

states.name: Palestine
timeline: The Judaean hill country and Jericho under the high priest Hyrcanus II
Parthian troops and their king Antigonus hold the Judaean hills
Herod takes the country after a long war against Antigonus
Cleopatra receives the palm and balsam groves of Jericho; Herod must lease them back
Octavian gives Jericho back to Herod

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre and Sidon govern themselves as free cities under Rome; Berytus, Byblos and Tripolis answer to the governor of Syria, Ituraean princes hold the Beqaa
Caesar passes along the coast and takes the treasures of Melqart's temple at Tyre
Cassius squeezes the coast for money; Marion becomes tyrant of Tyre
Antony orders Tyre to return the Galilean land Marion had seized
Pacorus's Parthians take Sidon and the whole coast; island Tyre alone holds out
Ventidius drives the Parthians back across the Euphrates; Tyre and Sidon are free again
Antony gives Cleopatra the coast from the Eleutherus to Egypt and the Ituraean lands of Chalcis, everything except Tyre and Sidon, which stay free
At the Donations of Alexandria, Phoenicia is proclaimed the kingdom of Ptolemy Philadelphus
Octavian returns the coast to the province of Syria; Tyre and Sidon keep their freedom until 20 BC

states.name: Syria
timeline: Rome's province of Syria, created by Pompey in 64 BC; Gabinius governs from Antioch
Crassus's army is destroyed at Carrhae; Cassius holds Syria with the survivors
Parthian raiders reach Antioch and are beaten back by Cassius
Caecilius Bassus raises a revolt and holds out in Apamea for three years
Cassius takes over Syria's legions; Dolabella dies at Laodicea
Pacorus and the Roman renegade Labienus overrun Syria; the governor Saxa is killed
Ventidius Bassus defeats the invaders and recovers Syria
Pacorus invades again and is killed at Mount Gindarus
The Donations name Ptolemy Philadelphus king of Syria, but Roman governors stay in charge
Octavian passes through on his way to Egypt

states.name: Libya
timeline: Cyrenaica, the Greek cities of eastern Libya, a Roman province since 74 BC
The Donations name Cleopatra Selene queen of Cyrenaica, but Antony's legate Pinarius Scarpus still governs
After Actium, Scarpus and his legions go over to Octavian

states.name: Jordan
timeline: The Nabataean kingdom of Petra; the Decapolis cities of the north belong to Roman Syria
Malichus I sends cavalry to help Caesar at Alexandria
Malichus turns the fugitive Herod away from Petra
Antony gives Cleopatra Nabataean lands and the Dead Sea's bitumen; Herod guarantees the rent
Herod defeats Malichus near Philadelphia (Amman)

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Gabinius restores Ptolemy XII; Roman troops, the Gabiniani, stay in Alexandria
Cleopatra VII, aged about eighteen, and her brother Ptolemy XIII inherit the throne
Civil war between Cleopatra and Ptolemy XIII; Caesar is besieged in Alexandria
Caesar's victory on the Nile leaves Cleopatra queen
After Caesar's murder, Cleopatra rules with her son Caesarion
The Donations of Alexandria proclaim Cleopatra Queen of Kings
Octavian takes Alexandria; Egypt becomes a Roman province

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Annexed by Rome in 58 BC and governed with the province of Cilicia
Caesar hands Cyprus back to the Ptolemies; it soon answers to Cleopatra
Cleopatra's governor Serapion sends the island's ships to help Cassius
Antony confirms Cyprus, with its copper and shipyards, as Cleopatra's
With Cleopatra dead, Cyprus returns to Roman rule

events.title: Pelusium falls
events.text: Gabinius's army crosses the Sinai; the young cavalry commander Mark Antony takes the border fortress of Pelusium.

events.title: The Piper restored
events.text: Ptolemy XII Auletes returns to Alexandria under Roman protection and has his daughter Berenice IV executed.

events.title: Temple looted
events.text: Crassus, the new governor of Syria, strips the Temple treasury in Jerusalem to pay for his war.

events.title: Carrhae
events.text: The Parthians destroy Crassus's army; Crassus is killed and his standards are lost.

events.title: Cleopatra's accession
events.text: Ptolemy XII dies; Cleopatra VII, about eighteen, shares the throne with her younger brother.

events.title: Raid on Antioch
events.text: A Parthian army reaches Antioch; Cassius holds the city and ambushes the raiders.

events.title: Pompey murdered
events.text: The defeated Pompey lands at Pelusium and is stabbed to death by Ptolemy XIII's courtiers.

events.title: Siege of the palace
events.text: Caesar, with Cleopatra at his side, is besieged in Alexandria's royal quarter through the winter.

events.title: Relief army
events.text: Mithridates of Pergamum and Antipater's Judaean troops storm Pelusium and march to Caesar's aid.

events.title: Battle of the Nile
events.text: Caesar defeats Ptolemy XIII, who drowns in the river; Cleopatra is confirmed as queen.

events.title: Caesar at Tyre
events.text: Marching north to Pontus, Caesar takes the offerings in Tyre's temple of Melqart.

events.title: Cyprus returned
events.text: Caesar gives Cyprus, annexed by Rome eleven years before, back to the Ptolemies.

events.title: Revolt at Apamea
events.text: Caecilius Bassus kills Syria's governor and holds Apamea against Caesar's generals.

events.title: Cleopatra goes home
events.text: After Caesar's murder in Rome, Cleopatra sails back to Alexandria with Caesarion.

events.title: Laodicea stormed
events.text: Cassius besieges Dolabella in Laodicea; the city falls and Dolabella takes his own life.

events.title: Marion expelled
events.text: Herod drives the forces of Marion, tyrant of Tyre, out of Galilee.

events.title: Tarsus
events.text: Cleopatra sails up the Cydnus to meet Antony, the new master of the East.

events.title: Antony at Tyre
events.text: Antony rejects a Judaean embassy against Herod and orders Tyre to give back Marion's conquests.

events.title: Raid on Palmyra
events.text: Antony's cavalry raids the desert city of Palmyra, whose merchants flee across the Euphrates.

events.title: Pacorus crosses
events.text: Prince Pacorus and the Roman renegade Quintus Labienus lead a Parthian army over the Euphrates.

events.title: Saxa defeated
events.text: Syria's governor Decidius Saxa is routed and killed; Antioch and Apamea open their gates.

events.title: Sidon surrenders
events.text: Sidon and Ptolemais submit to the Parthian cavalry without a fight.

events.title: Tyre holds out
events.text: Island Tyre, held by Roman refugees and its own citizens, cannot be taken by an army with no fleet.

events.title: Antigonus crowned
events.text: The Parthians make the Hasmonean Antigonus king in Jerusalem; Hyrcanus is mutilated and carried off.

events.title: Herod escapes
events.text: Herod leaves his family at Masada and flees by way of Petra and Alexandria to Rome.

events.title: Ventidius strikes
events.text: Antony's general Ventidius Bassus defeats Labienus and the Parthians in the Amanus passes.

events.title: Mount Gindarus
events.text: Pacorus returns with a new army and is killed; Parthia's grip on the West is broken.

events.title: Jerusalem taken
events.text: After a five-month siege, Herod and the Roman general Sosius storm Jerusalem.

events.title: The grants
events.text: Wintering in Antioch, Antony gives Cleopatra Phoenicia, Coele-Syria, Cyprus and Cilician timber for her fleet.

events.title: Chalcis given
events.text: Antony executes the Ituraean prince Lysanias and gives his realm under Mount Lebanon to Cleopatra.

events.title: White Village
events.text: Back from his failed Parthian war, Antony waits anxiously at Leuke Kome for Cleopatra's ships.

events.title: Jericho leased
events.text: Cleopatra visits Herod, who leases back his own balsam groves at Jericho for two hundred talents a year.

events.title: Donations of Alexandria
events.text: In the Gymnasium, Antony proclaims Cleopatra Queen of Kings and divides the East among her children.

events.title: Earthquake
events.text: A great earthquake devastates Judaea in the spring, killing thousands.

events.title: Herod and Malichus
events.text: Herod, kept out of Antony's war at Cleopatra's request, defeats the Nabataeans near Philadelphia.

events.title: Paraetonium
events.text: After the defeat at Actium, Antony lands here to find that the army of Cyrenaica has gone over to Octavian.

events.title: Herod changes sides
events.text: Herod welcomes Octavian's army at Ptolemais with supplies for the march into Egypt.

events.title: Pelusium opens
events.text: Octavian takes the gate of Egypt with hardly a fight.

events.title: Alexandria falls
events.text: On 1 August, Octavian enters Alexandria; Antony dies by his own sword.

events.title: Death of Cleopatra
events.text: Cleopatra takes her own life; Egypt becomes Rome's province and the Ptolemaic line ends.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries, by who held most of each in a given year; the regions are today's boundaries. A simplification: Lebanon stands for the Phoenician coast, where Tyre and Sidon stayed free while Antony gave the other cities to Cleopatra, and the vast Egyptian and Libyan deserts swing the shares. Grants made on paper at the Donations of Alexandria are noted but not coloured.
